diagnosis: Check C1 is leaking because it passes in every rollout despite the lone decision-maker only having access to S1, S3, and S4, while C1 depends on PF1 (which contains the specific 480-unit requirement). The model is defaulting to a standard production run of 900 units (the public value) and incorrectly triggering C1 as 'true' even though it failed to incorporate the hidden deviation.

C1.why: The customer deviation changes the provisional 900-unit run to exactly 480 units, changes inspection to 100% torque verification by two specified roles, and requires the deviation to be attached to the production order.

commitments.detail: Sunday electronics-assembly run for up to 900 units using an eight-hour shift.
Sunday electronics-assembly run for up to 900 units using an eight-hour shift.

fix_instructions: Tighten check C1 so that it only passes if the production_units decision exactly matches the value specified in PF1 (480 units), rather than allowing the default/public value of 900 units.
